result.summary: This is a narrow residential street with sidewalks on both sides and mature street trees providing shade. However, the environment lacks formal pedestrian infrastructure at the intersection, such as marked crosswalks, curb ramps, or traffic control devices.

hazards.name: Lack of marked crossings
hazards.description: There are no painted crosswalks at the intersection, making pedestrian movements less predictable for drivers.

hazards.name: Visual obstructions
hazards.description: Parked vehicles and dense foliage near the corner limit sightlines between pedestrians and approaching motorists.
hazards.location_in_image: Left side of the street near the foreground corner

hazards.name: Degraded pavement
hazards.description: Cracked and patched asphalt in the roadway and at the curb edge creates uneven surfaces.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install continental-style marked crosswalks to clearly define pedestrian right-of-way.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk at the corner to shorten crossing distance and improve visibility by moving pedestrians past parked cars.

interventions.title: ADA Compliant Curb Ramps
interventions.description: Install tactile warning strips and sloped ramps to ensure the crossing is accessible to all users.

result.summary: A narrow residential street with row houses and sidewalks on both sides. The environment lacks marked pedestrian crossings and visible traffic control at the immediate intersection, though the narrow roadway naturally limits vehicle speeds.

hazards.name: Unmarked Crossing
hazards.description: Lack of marked crosswalks at the intersection increases risk for pedestrians crossing the street.

hazards.name: Visibility Obstruction
hazards.description: The white vehicle positioned in the roadway may obstruct sightlines between drivers and pedestrians.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install continental-style marked crosswalks to clearly define pedestrian right-of-way.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces near the intersection to improve sightlines for both pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install bulb-outs at the corners to shorten crossing distances and slow turning vehicles.

result.summary: The image depicts a narrow, one-way residential street intersection with sidewalks in good condition. While the low traffic volume and narrow width are beneficial for safety, the lack of marked crosswalks and traffic control signage creates potential conflicts for pedestrians.

hazards.name: Unmarked Crossing
hazards.description: There is no marked crosswalk at the intersection to define pedestrian right-of-way.

hazards.name: Lack of Traffic Control
hazards.description: No stop or yield signs are visible to regulate vehicle entry into the intersection from the narrow street.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalk
interventions.description: Install continental-style crosswalk markings to clearly delineate the pedestrian path.

interventions.title: Stop Sign Installation
interventions.description: Add a stop sign for the narrow street to ensure vehicles yield to pedestrians and cross-traffic.

interventions.title: Raised Crosswalk
interventions.description: Implement a raised crosswalk to physically slow traffic and improve the visibility of pedestrians.
